analysis.title: GS Blekos - Marketcolour + Global 2027 Outlooks / Nvidia / Siemens / Richemont / Hermes / Wise
key_insights: US equities closed lower on 13 Nov 2026: SPX -35bps to 7592, NDX -30bps to 28289, RTY -166bps to 2799. 10 of 11 sectors fell, Consumer Discretionary -177bps, Energy +188bps, VIX +6.9% to 15.86.
Gold fell below $4,000/oz for the first time in months (XAU -2.7% to $3880). EU Miners fell 2% and EU Defense fell 2.4%. The GS Oil basket rose 1.30% and the Natural Gas basket rose 0.36%.

GS Global Macro 2027: global GDP grew 2.7% in 2026, in line with potential. GS expects 2.8% in 2027 as lower energy prices and strong AI capex outweigh tighter financial conditions and more neutral fiscal policy.

GS Global Equity Outlook 2027: overweight US and Japan, neutral Asia and EM, underweight Europe. Equities are expected to keep rising with high volatility, helped by more attractive valuations, lower bond yields, inflation and oil prices, and slower but positive nominal growth.

GS favors Growth balanced with selective Defensives and beneficiaries of lower bond yields. Long-duration Growth, especially US Hyperscalers, is favored because it becomes more valuable as growth rates slow and these companies keep strong earnings growth and balance sheets.

Nvidia (Buy, PT $220, 25% upside): GS expects a measured direct impact on financials and earnings power over 12-18 months from recent developments, given a 12-24 month backlog and order book and a roadmap for the next 2-3 years already in execution. The multiple is expected to be hit harder because of uncertainty.

Siemens (Buy, PT EUR308, 10% upside), management meeting takeaways: strong start to FY27 in automation, double-digit software growth expected for the year, data center growth visibility remains strong despite potential near-term order volatility and supply-chain dynamics, M&A discipline maintained, and Mobility is core to the AI strategy.

Ottobock (Buy, PT cut to EUR65 from EUR75, 60% upside): core revenue, EBITDA and EPS estimates cut by 0-6% for FY26/27/28e. GS wants clarity on whether the reimbursement challenges are transitory or structural.

Global Transport: the freight bull market continues in Q4. Global air and ocean freight volume growth is around high single digits. The US import surge looks set to taper in November, container freight rates are stable near historical highs, and European airlines are cutting capacity, especially short-haul.

Hermes (Sell, PT EUR1325, 5% downside): 2027 organic sales growth estimate cut to 6.1% from 7%, operating margin 40.3% versus 40.7% previously. At a 2027 PE of 27x with sales growth near the sector average, GS sees no upside. Q4 2026 sales growth expected around 4.4% y/y, in line with Q3.

Richemont: Jewellery Maisons Q2 sales grew 14% at constant FX versus consensus of 15.3% (buyside bar about 16%). The JM EBIT margin was 33.4% ex one-off, well ahead of sell-side consensus, implying more than 100bps ahead. The author thinks margin could drive the next leg higher but may not offset slower top-line growth given positioning.

Wise: results broadly in line with Street expectations. The Belgium overhang is removed with no admission of wrongdoing and an undisclosed settlement the author reads as immaterial. US licensing remediation is complete with an update expected in 2027, and the platform is launching quietly with two large US banks. The author expects the stock to rise.

2027 organic sales growth trimmed to 6.1%, close to the sector average, with shares at 27x 2027 PE leaving no upside. Hermes has no US listing named in the report.

GS Global Equity Outlook 2027 is underweight Europe, overweight US and Japan, neutral Asia and EM.

Wise (reported): results broadly in line with Street expectations. The Belgium matter is settled with the amount undisclosed. US licensing remediation is complete with an update expected in 2027.
